assumptions: Each row is one completed session; each session belongs to a different user.
Sessions are complete, so predictions are a visit simulation, not real-time scoring.
Identical rows are distinct single-page bounce sessions and are kept.
OperatingSystems, Browser, Region and TrafficType are anonymized category codes, not quantities.
constraints: No missing values in any column.
BounceRates, ExitRates and SpecialDay are within [0, 1].
Categorical columns contain only the listed allowed_values.
PageValues is strongly tied to the purchase outcome; the main model must not use it.

Administrative.meaning: Number of account-management pages the visitor viewed in the session.
Administrative.how_to_use: Use as a feature representing user interaction with account-management pages; integer values >= 0.

Administrative_Duration.meaning: Total seconds spent on account-management pages in the session.
Administrative_Duration.how_to_use: Use as a feature representing time spent on account-management pages; float values >= 0.

Informational.meaning: Number of informational pages (about the site, contact, policies) viewed in the session.
Informational.how_to_use: Use as a feature representing user interaction with informational pages; integer values >= 0.

Informational_Duration.meaning: Total seconds spent on informational pages in the session.
Informational_Duration.how_to_use: Use as a feature representing time spent on informational pages; float values >= 0.

ProductRelated.meaning: Number of product pages viewed in the session.
ProductRelated.how_to_use: Use as a feature representing user interest in products; integer values >= 0.

ProductRelated_Duration.meaning: Total seconds spent on product pages in the session.
ProductRelated_Duration.how_to_use: Use as a feature representing time spent on product pages; float values >= 0.

BounceRates.meaning: Average bounce rate (Google Analytics) of the pages viewed: share of visitors who entered on that page and left without another request.
BounceRates.how_to_use: Use as a feature representing page bounce behavior; float values within [0, 1].

ExitRates.meaning: Average exit rate (Google Analytics) of the pages viewed: share of page views that were the last of their session.
ExitRates.how_to_use: Use as a feature representing page exit behavior; float values within [0, 1].

PageValues.meaning: Average Google Analytics page value of the pages viewed before a completed transaction.
PageValues.how_to_use: Exclude from the main model as it strongly leaks the purchase outcome.

SpecialDay.meaning: Closeness of the visit date to a special day such as Mother's Day or Valentine's Day, from 0 (not close) to 1 (closest).
SpecialDay.how_to_use: Use as a feature indicating temporal proximity to special days; float values within [0, 1].

Month.how_to_use: Use as a categorical feature with allowed values: Feb, Mar, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec.

OperatingSystems.meaning: Anonymized code of the visitor's operating system.
OperatingSystems.how_to_use: Use as a categorical feature with allowed codes 1 to 8; these are category codes, not quantities.

Browser.meaning: Anonymized code of the visitor's browser.
Browser.how_to_use: Use as a categorical feature with allowed codes 1 to 13; these are category codes, not quantities.

Region.meaning: Anonymized code of the visitor's region.
Region.how_to_use: Use as a categorical feature with allowed codes 1 to 9; these are category codes, not quantities.

TrafficType.meaning: Anonymized code of the traffic source that brought the visitor (e.g. direct, banner, SMS).
TrafficType.how_to_use: Use as a categorical feature with allowed codes 1 to 20; these are category codes, not quantities.

VisitorType.meaning: Whether the visitor is new, returning or other.
VisitorType.how_to_use: Use as a categorical feature with allowed values: New_Visitor, Other, Returning_Visitor.

Weekend.meaning: Whether the visit happened on a weekend.
Weekend.how_to_use: Use as a boolean feature with values False or True.

Revenue.meaning: Whether the session ended in a purchase.
Revenue.how_to_use: Use as the prediction target; boolean values False or True.
